title: Japan national CPI (August 2026) — publishes 08:30 JST on BoJ decision day, hours before the MPM verdict
source: EST: stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/1582.html ('Consumer Price Index — Schedule of Release', page's own 'Last Update : 23 January 2026'), fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200) during the boj-decision-2026-09-18 pulse-check adjacency sweep. The page carries one release-schedule table whose column pairing is [Ku-area of Tokyo (preliminary) survey month | Tokyo date of release | Japan survey month | Japan date of release | Remarks]; on that pairing the row reading 'August | August 28 | ... | August | September 18' gives the Japan NATIONAL August-2026 CPI releasing 2026-09-18. The pairing is not asserted from this fetch alone — it is corroborated twice against the independent cell-by-cell parse recorded in japan-cpi-2026-11-20.json (Japan October -> November 20; Japan November -> December 18), both of which reproduce exactly under it and under no other alignment of the same rows. Release time 08:30 JST is the Statistics Bureau's standing rule and is NOT read off this page; it is carried here as the convention every sibling japan-cpi-* entry uses and should be re-verified at close-out. Filed estimate on three counts, identical to every sibling Japanese entry: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: for US statistical agencies and no slot for Japan's Statistics Bureau, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the schedule page has not been refreshed since 2026-01-23.
notes: PROPOSED during the boj-decision-2026-09-18 interval-elapsed pulse (2026-09-15, D-3) and owned by that lane, per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md's one-file-per-owner rule (#1717). Filed for one specific reason rather than for series completeness: this print is the BoJ ledger's OWN registered data kill switch ('Japanese national core CPI printing at or above 2.0% before the decision'), and it lands 08:30 JST on 2026-09-18 — roughly three to four hours before the September 17-18 MPM publishes its Statement on Monetary Policy the same morning. The calendar already tracks the series from japan-cpi-2026-11-20 forward; the 09-18 instance was missing, which meant the single most decision-adjacent Japanese print of the quarter was untracked. Structurally this is the same pattern japan-cpi-2026-11-20.json documented for December (the national November print arrives 2026-12-18, day two of the December MPM) — September is the same shape, and the pair recurring twice in one quarter is why it is worth a calendar row rather than a footnote. Context for whoever researches it: realised national core CPI (ex fresh food) was 1.8% y/y in July 2026, below the 2% target for a sixth consecutive month, against a July Outlook Report projecting core 'clearly above 2 percent from the second half of fiscal 2026' with risks 'skewed to the upside' — so this print is the last realised observation before a decision priced at 98.25% on a per-meeting venue book (Polymarket, fetched 2026-09-15T16:39:40Z). One caveat recorded rather than resolved: Japan's 2025-base CPI revision began publishing with the August 2026 releases, and the 2020-base series runs in parallel through December 2026, so a year-on-year comparison spanning the changeover should name which base it is on. Impact is LOW for the reasons every Japanese macro entry on this calendar carries: symbols is empty, no house playbook is keyed to Japanese CPI, and the channel to this book's AI names runs through yen funding and global term premium, both second-order and both already owned by the FOMC ledgers. The 2026-09-18 US session is separately and heavily confounded — it is the SET settlement of a $6.2T triple-witching (opex-2026-09-18) two days after the FOMC (fomc-2026-09-16) — so nothing in that tape is attributable to a Tokyo print without ruling both out first.
